question.text: SEBI has prescribed maximum leverage limits for Category III AIFs in relation to Net Asset Value. Per Ch 12 and current SEBI framework, this maximum leverage is:

answer.text: 1x of NAV (i.e., no net leverage beyond equity).
There is no SEBI-prescribed maximum leverage — Managers self-impose.

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI has capped Cat III AIF leverage at 2x of NAV. Ch 12 references this in risk factors and leverage section. The Trap: A understates. B overstates. D is incorrect — there IS a prescribed cap. Cross-Exam Context: Leverage is Cat III specific — tested heavily in XIX-B (Cat III distributor). In XIX-C, Manager must know the cap AND operating sub-cap. Manager's Pro-Tip: Set an internal operating sub-cap (e.g., 1.5x) with a 1.8x 'escalation trigger' requiring CIO sign-off and a 2.0x 'hard stop'. Document the governance — LPs love to see controls tighter than the regulator.
